links.outcome: Whether pre-go-live simulation with nurses identified CDS improvements and training needs
links.effect: 6 simulation sessions with 17 nurses yielded four debriefing themes that informed CDS improvements, real-world enhancements, and training requirements before go-live.
links.quote: Standardized simulation testing procedures identified and informed the necessary CDS improvements, the enhancements needed for real-world use, and the training requirements to effectively prepare end-users for system go-live.

links.outcome: Whether end-user simulation testing revealed usability and workflow-fit issues to act on before implementation
links.effect: Simulation debriefs with 17 nurses produced four themes used to inform implementation strategies and how the CDS should be improved for practical real-world use.
links.quote: Four themes were extracted from the simulation debriefing sessions and used to inform implementation strategies.

screen.practice: Pre-implementation clinical simulation testing with end-users
screen.reason: The study empirically tests a standardized pre-implementation clinical simulation process with nurses to evaluate interpretability, usability, and workflow integration of an AI-based early warning risk score (CONCERN).
